Graph neural networks have become a foundational component of modern recommender systems, enabling the integration of relational data into user–item modeling [S2:f97aee2318d91d83672ce248c23f6d8ecc03bb8c]. Comprehensive surveys highlight the rapid expansion of GNN applications across personalized recommendation tasks, emphasizing their ability to capture high‑order connectivity and semantic similarity [S2:1be97c1d9ace0363f8f612ca1be3d4fb33e177bb].

Neural Graph Collaborative Filtering proposes a graph convolutional architecture that directly propagates user and item embeddings over the bipartite interaction graph, thereby enriching representations with high‑order collaborative signals [S2:c5f5f179d80a3bf9b4f29750283a87eaca42e91b].

Revisiting Graph based Collaborative Filtering introduces a linear residual graph convolutional network that simplifies the propagation mechanism while preserving performance, demonstrating that shallow residual connections can match deeper GCNs in recommendation accuracy [S2:c9e432023a240b22f385cf1cc76ab75fbe084ee7]. Profiling the Design Space for Graph Neural Networks based Collaborative Filtering systematically evaluates architectural choices such as layer depth, aggregation function, and embedding dimension, revealing that optimal configurations depend on dataset sparsity and interaction patterns [S2:a2a42052eb8c0dd5ee339877b37f135fdfea00bd].
